Last year the owner purchased a parcel of land immediately adjacent to the shopping center. The drugstore use on the adjacent parcel was in existence when the owner and the pharmacist firstentered into the lease.
The discount drugstore on the adjacent parcel is not considered a 'new' lease, but a continuation of an existing one.
A covenant cannot restrict the use of land not owned by the covenantor when the covenant wascreated.
The owner has the right to lease any part of his property to any business, regardless of existing leases.
The pharmacist did not adequately express his concerns to the owner before initiating legal action.
A covenant that attempts to restrict competition is invalid as against public policy even if it runs with theland.

question: A resident announced his candidacy for state representative. A law in the state requires new political entrants (regardless of party affiliation) to obtain three times the number of signatures as other candidates who have run for office previously. The resident, however, failed to obtain the necessary number of authenticating signatures to have his name placed on the ballot. The resident filed a complaint in federal district court alleging the unconstitutionality of the authenticating requirement. Which of the following, if established, is the state's strongest argument for sustaining the validity of the authenticating requirement?
options: A similar authenticating statute was held to be constitutional in another state the previous year.
Other states also have similar authenticating requirements.
The authenticating requirement ensures that only serious and committed candidates run for office.
The resident did not actively campaign to get the necessary signatures.
The authenticating requirement was introduced to reduce the number of frivolous candidates.
The authenticating requirement was necessary to further a compelling state interest.
Two other candidates had successfully petitioned to have their names included on the ballot.
The resident has a history of fraudulent activities.
The resident could have obtained the necessary signatures if he had started collecting them earlier.
The resident's petition contained a large number of false signatures.
gold: The authenticating requirement was necessary to further a compelling state interest.
